title: `PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR` sometimes changes `PropertyHint` and associated hint string
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in v4.0.4.stable.official, v4.5.1.stable.official, v4.6.rc1.official ### System information W11 ### Issue description I don't know if this is a bug or if it is working as intended. It always has done a variation of this since 4.0. When viewing `PropertyHint` via `get_property_list()`, the `PropertyUsageFlag` `PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR` will change the `PropertyHint` of certain variables. I'm almost certain its `PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR` because I compared variables like this: ```GDScript var ArrayString1: Array[String] @export_storage var ArrayString2: Array[String] @export var ArrayString3: Array[String] ``` and have found that `@export_storage` acts the same as a standard variable, but `@export` differs. ## Observations (from `var` to `@export var`) - Most types are uninteresting at hint = 0 with empty string going unchanged - Ints of a Named enum go from hint = 0 with empty string to hint = 2 with the appropriate string - Nodes go from hint = 0 with empty string to hint = 34 with appropriate string - Resources go from hint = 0 with empty string to hint = 17 with appropriate string - Typed Dictionaries go from hint = 38 with appropriate human-readable string to hint = 23 with less-readable, appropriate string - Typed Arrays go from hint = 31 with appropriate human-readable string to hint = 23 with less-readable, appropriate string - Packed Arrays go from hint = 0 with empty string to hint = 23 with less-readable, appropriate string ## Expectations I expected them to be the same regardless of exporting or not. However, I can see why they'd change for the benefit of the inspector when used in the editor (adding to my uncertainty of its bug status). I began my observation after I tried searching an int of a named enum via `hint == PROPERTY_HINT_ENUM` in `get_property_list()` and I couldn't find it (non-exported), after having done so before and finding it (exported). ### Steps to reproduce 1. Import MRP 2. Run Scene 3. Observe Outputs Example of Outputs truncated: ``` Hint format {hint: hint_string} var -> @export var bool: { 0: "" } -> { 0: "" } int: { 0: "" } -> { 0: "" } enum: { 0: "" } -> { 2: "Value 1:0,Value 2:1" } ... ``` Notice enum has changed. Also For the purpose of the enum I had: ```GDScript enum MyEnum { VALUE1, VALUE2, } ... var enum1: MyEnum @export_storage var enum2: MyEnum @export var enum3: MyEnum ``` If you wish to verify that `@export_storage` does nothing, uncomment line 106 and 112 The output format changes to: ``` Hint format {hint: hint_string} var -> @export_storage var -> @export var bool: { 0: "" } -> { 0: "" } -> { 0: "" } int: { 0: "" } -> { 0: "" } -> { 0: "" } enum: { 0: "" } -> { 0: "" } -> { 2: "Value 1:0,Value 2:1" } ... ``` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) for 4.0 onward: [prop-hint-mrp-4.0.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24693796/prop-hint-mrp-4.0.zip) This MRP has no `@export_storage` nor typed dictionary for 4.3 onward: [prop-hint-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24693747/prop-hint-mrp.zip) This MRP has `@export_storage` and typed dictionaries (**Must** comment out the typed dictionaries if testing 4.3)
